ChatGPT has never seen a single letter you typed.
First, your sentence is chopped into pieces called tokens.
Common words stay whole. Rare words get split into smaller chunks.
A word like unbelievably might become three pieces: un, believ, and ably.
A tokenizer learns those chunks by merging the letter pairs that show up together most often.
Each chunk then becomes a number, an ID in a vocabulary of tens of thousands.
The model only ever sees those numbers, never the letters inside them.
That's one reason counting the R's in strawberry can trip it up.
And it's why limits are counted in tokens, not words.
